paragraphs: At lunch, Lily, Mia, and Leo sat at a table near the school hall. A poster on the wall said, "School Show. Friday. Six o'clock." "I am going to sell tickets after school," said Mia. "What is the price of a ticket?" asked Lily. "It is ten baht," said Mia. "But there is a discount for families." "Three tickets cost only twenty baht." "Mom will buy three, so we will get the discount," said Lily.

"Where will you put the money?" asked Leo. "I will put it in this envelope," said Mia. She held up a big brown envelope. "Teacher Kim will check the money on Friday." "Please write 'Show Money' on it," said Leo. "I will," said Mia. "Then nobody will lose it."

"What are you going to do on the stage, Leo?" asked Lily. Leo smiled and said, "I am going to be a pirate in a bathtub boat." "A bathtub boat?" said Mia. "Yes," said Leo. "My home has an old bathtub, but it is too heavy." "So I will make a bathtub from boxes." "I need a lot of stuff: paper, paint, and a big box." "That is a funny idea," said Lily. "Will it float?" "It does not have to float," said Leo. "It is going to stand on the stage."

Teacher Kim came with some papers in her hand. "This is the program for the show," she said. "It tells the order of the acts." Lily read the program carefully. "The school band will play first," she said. "Then our class will do a dance, and Leo's boat is next." "Our class will perform one more song at the end," said Teacher Kim. "Who will give the programs to the visitors at the door?" "We will," said Lily and Mia.

"What time will we meet on Friday?" asked Leo. "At half past five in the hall," said Teacher Kim. "I will bring the bathtub boat and my pirate hat," said Leo. "Tickets are cheap, so the hall will be full," said Mia. "Then Friday will be a great evening," said Teacher Kim.
